description: A run handed from agent to agent as ONE chain: a labelled step per handoff — who handed what to whom, when, how the receiving agent answered — with the things that travelled and the things that were lost (and why) behind a Details button on every step, plus a chain-wide loss summary that names what the run actually dropped. The surface renders the steps it is given and never polls or mutates anything: the host owns the handoff data and the transport, the component owns its view. The step ordering is the host's own chain order — the component never reorders, filters or invents a step. Accessibility: the chain is an ordered list of labelled steps, every status and every item kind is an ICON plus a localized WORD plus a tone (colour is never the only carrier, WCAG 1.4.1), and the passed/lost lists live in a region a native <button> opens and closes with aria-expanded and aria-controls — no key emulation anywhere (docs/keyboard-activation-convention.md). The table view carries exactly the same facts without the geometry, so a screen-reader, keyboard-only or phone reader loses nothing. ONE polite live region speaks only when a step the reader was on disappears from the host's data and the focus has to move.

parameters.name: Class
parameters.description: Additional CSS class(es) for the root element.

parameters.name: Culture
parameters.description: The culture that formats the handoff times. Null (the default) means the current culture at render time.

parameters.name: ExpandedStepIds
parameters.description: The ids of the steps whose detail is open, two-way bound with ExpandedStepIdsChanged. Null (the default) means EVERY step is open, because the passed and lost lists are the reason to look at a chain at all; an empty list closes them all. A host that pins the list keeps control: the reader's toggle reports the new set and the next render decides.

parameters.name: ExpandedStepIdsChanged
parameters.description: Fires with the new expanded set when the reader opens or closes a step's detail.

parameters.name: HeadingLevel
parameters.description: The heading level of the rendered title, clamped to 2–6. Default 3.

parameters.name: Orientation
parameters.description: Which way the chain runs. Default Vertical. The orientation is a layout hook on the root — both values render the same ordered list, so nothing is lost when a narrow card turns the chain on its side.

parameters.name: ShowSummary
parameters.description: Whether the summary block is rendered. Default true. It carries the settled / total handoff count, the passed and lost totals, the loss rate and whether anything is still pending.

parameters.name: ShowTitle
parameters.description: Whether the heading is rendered. Default true.

parameters.name: Steps
parameters.description: The handoffs, in chain order. Each entry is one step; null or empty renders the localized empty state, and a null entry inside the list is skipped. The component never mutates or reorders the list.

parameters.name: Title
parameters.description: The heading above the surface. Null renders the localized default ("Agent handoffs"); the heading also names the surface, so the name a reader hears is the one they see.

parameters.name: ViewMode
parameters.description: The presentation, two-way bound with ViewModeChanged (@bind-ViewMode). Default Chain. Table renders the same steps as one table, which is the text alternative of the chain.

parameters.name: ViewModeChanged
parameters.description: Fires with the new presentation when the reader uses the View switcher.

notes: The surface renders the steps it is given; it never polls, fetches or mutates a handoff.
A state and an item kind are always an icon AND a localized word AND a tone, never a colour alone (WCAG 1.4.1).
The passed and lost lists live in a region a native button opens and closes (aria-expanded + aria-controls); ExpandedStepIds = null opens every step, an empty list closes them all.
The table view (ViewMode=Table) carries every step, item label and loss reason as text — the chain is never the only way to read the data.
One polite live region speaks only when a step the reader was on disappears from the host data and the focus has to move.
